In the Flask ecosystem, flasgger is a popular extension that integrates Swagger UI into your application, allowing you to generate interactive API documentation using OpenAPI specifications."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Installation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"To get started, you need to install Flask and Flasgger. Run the following command in your terminal:"},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install flask flasgger"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Setting Up the Flask Application"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Next, create your main application file (e.g., app.py) and initialize Flask along with the Swagger extension. Flasgger will automatically serve the Swagger UI interface at the /apidocs/ endpoint."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask, jsonify, request
from flasgger import Swagger

app = Flask(__name__)
swagger = Swagger(app)

@app.route('/api/item', methods=['GET'])
def get_item():
    """
    Get a sample item
    ---
    responses:
      200:
        description: A successful response
        schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            message:
              type: string
              example: Hello, Swagger!
    """
    return jsonify({"message": "Hello, Swagger!"})

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(debug=True)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Adding Parameters and Request Bodies"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also document POST endpoints that accept parameters or JSON payloads by expanding the docstring YAML specification."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"@app.route('/api/item', methods=['POST'])
def create_item():
    """
    Create a new item
    ---
    parameters:
      - name: body
        in: body
        required: true
        schema:
          id: item
          required:
            - name
          properties:
            name:
              type: string
              description: The name of the item
    responses:
      201:
        description: Item created successfully
    """
    data = request.json
    return jsonify({"status": "success", "name": data.get("name")}), 201"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Flask and Swagger"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep docstrings clean by separating large OpenAPI definitions into external YAML files."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always define expected response schemas to help frontend developers understand the data contract."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Secure your /apidocs/ endpoint in production environments to prevent exposing internal routes."}]
